about: Catalogue passages every contract of batch 1 answers the same way (Part 6 common, Part 1 shared rules, the supplement's conventions and gates), with how each is met. Each contract lists its own passages; the conformance test (lib/forms/catalogue-contracts.test.ts) checks both against the documents.

quotes: The central architectural rule is clinical confidentiality by design.
CivicOS may provide common identity, case management, payments, notifications, and audit infrastructure, but clinical records must remain under the control of authorized health institutions.
A government-wide platform must not become a universal medical-record browser.

quotes: On scanning, store the original scan, the extraction result and any human correction as separate evidence.
OCR output is a proposed transcription, never a verified fact until the required review is complete.
Additional channels: field capture, offline submission and USSD/SMS are enabled only when appropriate to the service.
A short-message interface must not collect documents or sensitive details that its security model cannot safely handle.

Offline capture must record the capture time, submitting actor, device or session provenance and synchronization state; conflicting submissions must be resolved through an explicit, auditable workflow, never by silently overwriting the record.
Before a form can be approved, CivicOS must run a field-level minimisation review.
What decision, action or statutory record requires this information?
Which legal provision or approved procedural requirement authorizes its collection?
Is it already available through an authorized register or exchange?
Can the purpose be achieved with less sensitive data?
Who can read it, for what purpose, and for how long?
What happens if the applicant cannot supply it?
Is the field necessary in all cases, or only under a registered condition?
A required field without a satisfactory answer must block approval.
A special-category field requires stronger justification and narrower access.
An exchange lookup must be denied unless both the requesting institution and the purpose are authorized.
Logging a read is mandatory but does not make an otherwise unauthorized read lawful.
